findings.title: Source gate accepts unmanifested build inputs
findings.counterexample: Executed delivered checker in a temporary valid manifest fixture, then added an unlisted root vite.config.js. The checker exited 0 and reported PASS/fileCount 7. Installed Vite resolves vite.config.js before vite.config.ts, so this extra file can change build behavior while listed bytes stay unchanged.
findings.evidence: Deterministic local fixture, not a hypothesis. The checker only iterates files formed from manifest maps; it never compares that set with the actual releasable source inventory.
findings.minimalCorrection: Enumerate actual releasable files before checks and require exact equality with manifest entries plus RELEASE-MANIFEST.json. Use an explicit exclusion list for .git, dependencies, generated build/test artifacts; preserve the repository-workflow policy explicitly if extra existing workflows are intentionally exempt.
findings.regressionExpectation: A valid release passes; adding vite.config.js, a public asset, or an unlisted source file fails; approved local output directories remain excluded.

findings.title: Hosted identity is not bound to the returned application bytes
findings.counterexample: Executed the exact delivered hosted-smoke Bash with deterministic curl responses: a 1.3.1 HTML page referencing old.js, a 1.3.1 worker containing EQUINOX/ACTIVATE_UPDATE, a valid scoped manifest, and current 1.3.2 release.json with the expected SHA. Script exited 0.
findings.evidence: The gate checks exact identity only in release.json. HTML and worker checks are generic string matches and cannot establish that those returned bytes belong to the tested revision. This demonstrates a gate false-positive, not an actual stale deployment.
findings.minimalCorrection: Generate expected hashes from the final repository-path build, carry them from verify to deploy, and compare downloaded HTML, manifest, worker and application entry assets against those expected bytes. Keep commit/app identity as an additional assertion.
findings.regressionExpectation: Exact deployed artifact passes; a current release.json paired with old HTML, worker, JS or CSS fails.
